item.title: Rome: The City of Seven Hills
item.description:
A single narrator tells the story of Rome from the seven hills beside the Tiber. It begins with the Romulus legend as legend, early kings and the Republic, then aqueducts, the Forum, the Colosseum, and the Pantheon. After a gentle pass through later papal and Italian Rome, it ends with evening among the stones of the Forum.

item.title: Paris: The Island in the River
item.description:
A single narrator tells the story of Paris from its river islands outward. It begins with the Seine and the Parisii settlement of Lutetia, then Clovis and the Capetians, Notre-Dame, the Louvre fortress, and the Left Bank schools. After a light touch on revolutionary storms, it covers Haussmann's boulevards and the Eiffel Tower, and ends with evening on the quays.

item.title: New York: The Harbour of Arrivals
item.description:
A single narrator tells the story of New York City as a harbour town that grew into a metropolis. It begins with the harbour and the Lenape shore, then Verrazzano and Henry Hudson, Dutch New Amsterdam, and the English takeover in 1664. After that come the Revolution and Washington's inauguration, the Erie Canal, the 1811 grid, the Brooklyn Bridge, Central Park, the Statue of Liberty, Ellis Island, and the five-borough consolidation of 1898. It ends with evening on the harbour.

Walking the Tip of the Island; 9. Five Boroughs, One Harbour; 10. Markets, Ferries, and Daily Bread; 11. The Grid Fills In; 12. Bridges, Tunnels, and the Modern Port; 13. Soft City Nights; 14. Names on the Land; 15. Evening on the Harbour.

item.title: The Great Wall: Many Walls
item.description:
A single narrator tells the story of the Great Wall of China, which is really many walls built over two thousand years. It begins with the Ming frontier's most dramatic moments: the capture of an emperor at Tumu in 1449, Altan Khan's raid of 1550 and the peace that followed, and the opening of Shanhaiguan in 1644. Then it goes back to rammed-earth walls, the Qin and Han frontiers, and soldiers' letters on wooden strips. After that come the beacon towers, the walls between the dynasties, the Cloud Platform at Juyongguan, Qi Jiguang's brick towers, and travellers such as Xuanzang and the Macartney embassy. It also covers Jiayuguan and a few myths, including whether the Wall is visible from space. It ends with evening on a quiet stretch of the wall.
Chapters: 1. Many Walls; 2. The Emperor Who Was Captured; 3. Raiders at the Gates; 4. The Gate by the Sea; 5. Earth Between Boards; 6. The Han Frontier; 7. Letters on Wood; 8. Signals Across the Hills; 9. Between the Dynasties; 10. Soldiers from the South; 11. Brick and Stone; 12. Travellers at the Gates; 13. A Few Old Stories; 14. The Fortress in the West; 15. The Wall Today; 16. Walking the Wall; 17. Along the Line; 18. Evening on the Wall.

item.title: Alexandria: The Library by the Sea
item.description:
A single narrator tells the story of the Library of Alexandria. It begins with the question of how the library ended: Caesar's fire, Aurelian's war, the Serapeum, Hypatia and a later legend. None of these alone tells the whole story. Then the debate over how many books it held. After that the episode goes back to Alexander's founding of the city, its streets and harbours, the Pharos lighthouse, and the Museum and its scholars, from Callimachus's catalogue to Eratosthenes measuring the Earth. Later it visits the Serapeum, the catacombs of Kom el Shoqafa, the papyri of Oxyrhynchus and the new Bibliotheca Alexandrina. It ends with evening on the harbour.
Chapters: 1. A Library by the Sea; 2. How Did It End?; 3. How Many Books?; 4. The City of Alexander; 5. Streets of Alexandria; 6. The Lighthouse; 7. The Museum; 8. Collecting the World; 9. The Librarians; 10. Measuring the Earth; 11. Scholars of the Museum; 12. The Temple of Serapis; 13. The Last of the Ptolemies; 14. Beneath the City; 15. Books in the Sand; 16. The New Library; 17. Evening on the Harbour.

item.title: Angkor: The City in the Forest
item.description:
A single narrator tells the story of Angkor, the great capital of the Khmer Empire in Cambodia. It begins with the Cham attack of 1177 and the rise of Jayavarman VII, who built Angkor Thom and the Bayon with its calm stone faces. Then the long, gradual fading of the capital, where historians still debate the causes. After that the episode goes back to the beginnings: Phnom Kulen, the brick towers of Roluos, and the barays and canals revealed by lidar. It goes on to the island shrine of Neak Pean, Banteay Srei, Angkor Wat and its carvings, and the account of the Chinese envoy Zhou Daguan. It ends in daily life and evening among the temples.
Chapters: 1. The City in the Forest; 2. Fire on the Lake; 3. A New Capital; 4. The Long Fading; 5. Never Quite Lost; 6. Beginnings on the Mountain; 7. The Sacred Bull; 8. Water; 9. The Island in the Pool; 10. The Citadel of Women; 11. The Temple of Vishnu; 12. Stories in Stone; 13. A Visitor from China; 14. Daily Life; 15. Evening at Angkor.

item.title: Pompeii: The Town Beneath the Mountain
item.description:
A single narrator tells the story of Pompeii, the Roman town on the Bay of Naples. It begins with the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79 and the eyewitness letters of Pliny the Younger, including the death of his uncle, Pliny the Elder, at Stabiae. Then the debate over the date: August or October? After that the episode slows into the centuries the town lay buried, its rediscovery, Fiorelli's plaster casts and the site today. It ends in quiet daily life: the streets, fountains and bakeries, the election notices and graffiti, the baths and amphitheatre, the houses and gardens, and evening on the bay.
Chapters: 1. A Town Beneath the Mountain; 2. The Mountain; 3. The Letters of Pliny; 4. Darkness at Misenum; 5. What the Volcano Did; 6. Which Day?; 7. Asleep for Centuries; 8. The Shapes in the Ash; 9. Pompeii Today; 10. Streets, Water and Bread; 11. Walls That Talk; 12. Temples, Baths and Games; 13. Houses and Gardens; 14. Evening on the Bay.

item.title: Machu Picchu, Part 3: The Quiet Centuries
item.description:
Part 3 of 3. Henry and Clara follow Machu Picchu from the fall of the Inca empire to today: the epidemic and civil war, Pizarro and Cajamarca, Manco Inca's last refuge at Vilcabamba, and why the estate emptied with no sign the Spanish ever found it. Cusco rebuilt on Inca walls. Three quiet centuries of forest and farmers, early maps, the debated Berns story, and Agustín Lizárraga's charcoal "1902" on the Temple of the Three Windows. Then the damp morning of 24 July 1911: Melchor Arteaga, Sergeant Carrasco, the Richarte and Álvarez families, a local boy leading Hiram Bingham to the ruins, and the real Vilcabamba he walked past. Who gets the credit, Yale's century-long hold on the artifacts and their return to Cusco's Casa Concha, and Machu Picchu now: UNESCO, timed tickets, llamas, orchids and spectacled bears. Debated points (the city's original name, Berns, why it was abandoned) are gently flagged. Next on Slow History: Pompeii.
Chapters: 1. Settling In; 2. The Empire Breaks; 3. The Last Inca Refuge; 4. Cusco Under New Rulers; 5. The Quiet Centuries; 6. A Damp Morning in July; 7. Digging and Telling; 8. Who Gets the Credit?; 9. The Long Way Home; 10. Machu Picchu Today; 11. Goodnight, Machu Picchu.

item.title: Machu Picchu, Part 2: Inside the City in the Clouds
item.description:
Part 2 of 3. Henry and Clara walk slowly through Machu Picchu: in through the main gate, to the curved Temple of the Sun and its June-solstice window, the quiet cave below, the royal rooms by the first fountain, the quarry, the Sacred Plaza and the Temple of the Three Windows, and the carved Intihuatana (whose name and purpose are still debated). Then the people: a 2023 ancient-DNA study shows the estate's attendants came from all over the Inca world, from the coast to the Amazon. A gentle imagined day on the ridge, the Temple of the Condor, and out along the Inca roads to the Sun Gate. Next: Part 3, the quiet centuries and how the world came to hear of it.

Who Lived Here?; 9. A Day on the Ridge; 10. The Condor and the Moon; 11. The Roads Out; 12. Slowly Down the Mountain.

item.title: Machu Picchu, Part 1: The Earth-Shaker's Estate in the Clouds
item.description:
Part 1 of 3. Henry and Clara drift up to the misty ridge between the old peak and the young peak, and meet Pachacuti, "the one who turns the world." Who the Inca were, how Machu Picchu is tied to Pachacuti's royal estate (a 1568 Spanish record of his lands at "Picchu"), the 2021 radiocarbon dates that suggest people lived there by about 1420, and how the builders tamed the rain with buried drainage, layered terraces, a spring-fed canal and sixteen stepped fountains. Terrace restorer Tomás phones in softly. Uncertain history (dates, the original name, population) is gently marked as debated. Quiet mountain wind, a distant stream and a soft Andean flute between chapters. Next: Part 2, inside the city. Part 3, the quiet years, Bingham in 1911, and Machu Picchu today.
Chapters: 1. Settling In; 2. The Ridge Between Two Peaks; 3. The People of the Sun; 4. Pachacuti, the Earth-Shaker; 5. An Estate in the Clouds; 6. When Was It Built?; 7. How Do You Build on a Mountain?; 8. A Call from the Terraces; 9. The Water That Still Flows; 10. Planning the City; 11. Slowly Down the Mountain.

item.title: Shenzhen, Part 3: The City of Arrivals

Part 3 of 3.

item.title: Shenzhen, Part 1: The County by the Sea
item.description:
Thomas and Clara drift back through sixteen centuries on the coast that became Shenzhen: Nantou and the salt fields, the walled towns of 1394, Xin'an county, the Great Clearance, Hakka and Cantonese villages, the Opium Wars and the new Hong Kong border, and the little railway market town called Shenzhen. Part 1 of 3.

Chapters: 1. Settling in; 2. The edge of the delta; 3. Nantou, the old seat; 4. Walls against the pirates; 5. Xin'an, a new county; 6. The great clearance; 7. Hakka and Cantonese villages; 8. Ships on the horizon; 9. A railway and a market town; 10. Not just a fishing village; 11. Goodnight.
